feed.subtitle: Research papers and global crypto regulation, at a glance
feed.rights: Explanations and summaries are generated by AI from the original text. Dates, rates and amounts are checked against the source, but errors are still possible, so always rely on the original. Nothing here is legal, tax or investment advice.

entry.title: Exact analytical solution for collectively pumped superradiance in Dicke states
entry.summary: Exact Analytical Treatment of Collectively Pumped Dicke Superradiance arXiv · Oct 28, 2026 This paper studies a group of N two-level emitters that decay collectively and are pumped collectively, staying within the symmetric Dicke states. The authors sum up the infinitely many quantum trajectories created by competing pumping and decay to obtain an exact finite continued fraction for the Dicke-state populations. They also give perturbative transient solutions for strong and weak pumping, along with relaxation eigenvalues and emission observables for balanced pumping and decay.

entry.title: Optimal quantum discrimination at Liouvillian exceptional points
entry.summary: Optimal quantum discrimination at Liouvillian exceptional points arXiv · Oct 28, 2026 This paper examines whether exceptional points (EPs) in non-Hermitian systems help detect weak perturbations. In finite-dimensional Lindblad systems with a unique stationary state and nonzero relaxation gap, the authors show EPs give no fundamental advantage in how observation time scales with perturbation strength. However, by selecting perturbations that boost the quantum Fisher information rate, EPs can reach a set detection accuracy faster than a non-EP reference with the same decay rate. An optomechanical model illustrates detecting a weak force at an EP in less time.

entry.title: Repulsive Landau Interactions Between Fermi Polarons at Strong Coupling
entry.summary: Mediated Interactions between Fermi Polarons in the Strongly Interacting Regime arXiv · Oct 28, 2026 This paper studies mediated interactions between quasiparticles emerging from a Fermi sea, known as Fermi polarons, using zero-temperature quantum Monte Carlo methods. The main result is that the Landau interaction between polarons stays repulsive across all coupling strengths on the polaronic branch in the strongly interacting regime. The authors also compute the real-space interaction between static impurities, which shows RKKY-like behavior at weak coupling and matches the nonperturbative Born-Oppenheimer result at strong coupling. ★★★★ Notable: Zero-temperature quantum Monte Carlo reveals repulsive polaron-polaron interactions at strong coupling, contrasting experiments and recovering RKKY and Born-Oppenheimer limits.

entry.title: Dynamical quantum simulations used as testbeds for quantum information
entry.summary: Dynamical quantum simulations as laboratories for quantum information arXiv · Oct 28, 2026 This paper shows that dynamical quantum simulations built to compute response functions prepare many-body states that carry information beyond their original observable. Using local-pulse protocols for Green functions in finite XX and XXX spin chains as a case study, the authors encode a classical bit via opposite source rotations and track how this record spreads across local subsystems and how readily different measurements access it. They find that fermionic covariance reconstructs the signed response in the XX chain, while simple spin measurements recover more local information in the XXX chain. The analysis is extended to Bell state recovery, quantum communication rates, and bipartite and multipartite entanglement.

entry.title: Meet-in-the-Middle Compilation of the [CNOT] Class with Fibonacci Anyons
entry.summary: Meet-in-the-Middle Compilation of the [CNOT] Class with Fibonacci Anyons arXiv · Oct 28, 2026 This paper studies how to compile two-qubit gates for Fibonacci anyons, where errors arise from leakage out of the computational subspace into a fifth fusion state. The authors build a GPU pipeline that searches braid group subsets for low-leakage representatives of the [CNOT] class, narrowing the search space to reach braid length L=72. They prove that leakage lies in Z[φ], that nonzero leakage has an exponential lower bound in braid length, and derive limit distribution laws.

entry.title: Recovering classical gauge geometry from quantum master constraints
entry.summary: Recovering classical gauge geometry from quantum master constraints arXiv · Oct 28, 2026 The paper asks how the degenerate directions of classical first-class constraints can be recovered when quantum theory is taken as fundamental and the constraints are imposed through a single positive master operator. For a nonnegative master function whose zero set is a Morse–Bott critical manifold, the image of the linearized Hamiltonian vector field is shown to be the symplectic orthogonal of the zero set, with coisotropy equivalent to the linearization having square zero. Three realizations are discussed, including the spectral bottom for quadratic masters and results for the non-Abelian SL(2,R) model.

entry.title: Adaptive Information Mining: Reaching the Quantum Limit of Super-Resolution Imaging
entry.summary: Adaptive Information Mining: Approaching the Quantum Limit of Super-Resolution Imaging arXiv · Oct 28, 2026 This paper presents Adaptive Information Mining (AIM), a framework that achieves super-resolution by refining measurements of incoming photons in sequence. A reconfigurable imaging system reshapes its measurement responses to maximize Fisher information. When imaging point sources, the authors report estimation errors 2 to 5 times closer to the fundamental quantum limit than traditional direct imaging.

entry.title: Paper on homodyne-based tracking and parameter estimation for quantum systems in squeezed thermal baths.
entry.summary: Homodyne Unravelling and Parameter Estimation in Squeezed Thermal Baths arXiv · Oct 28, 2026 The paper derives an alternative stochastic master equation for quantum systems continuously measured by homodyne detection in a squeezed-thermal environment. This form identifies two collapse operators for monitored and unmonitored channels and expresses state evolution through Kraus-like operators, aiding numerical methods and Cramér-Rao bound evaluation. For qubit frequency estimation, the authors compute the Fisher information of continuous homodyne monitoring and find that its steady-state rate still scales exponentially with squeezing at nonzero temperature.

entry.title: Measurement incompatibility and noiseless quantum codes: a theory paper on whether quantum channels can preserve measurement incompatibility
entry.summary: Measurement incompatibility and noiseless quantum codes arXiv · Oct 27, 2026 The paper studies when a quantum channel universally preserves the incompatibility of measurements. The authors construct a rank-one minimal informationally complete measurement and prove that such preservation holds if and only if the input space contains a noiseless code subspace of full output dimension. They also give an explicit construction of exact encodings and connect the results to quantum steering and quantum error correction. ★★★★ Notable: Constructs a rank-one MIC and proves equivalence with noiseless codes, resolving a conjecture with thorough proofs; impact mainly within quantum information theory.

entry.title: Security analysis of an Ekert-type QKD protocol under cloning attacks
entry.summary: Security Analysis of Ekert-type QKD Protocol Coming Under Cloning Attacks arXiv · Oct 27, 2026 This paper analyzes the security of an Ekert-type bipartite key distribution protocol when an untrusted observer performs cloning attacks. An eavesdropper intercepts qubits sent over a public channel and applies an asymmetric, phase-variant cloner to one or both of them. The authors partially characterize two-qubit states and use the Devetak-Winter framework to compute key rates, identifying states from which a secret key can still be distilled under such attacks.

entry.title: Quantum key distribution secured by a bound on information leakage
entry.summary: Prepare-and-measure quantum key distribution from a bound on information leakage arXiv · Oct 27, 2026 This paper examines whether, in prepare-and-measure quantum key distribution, a single bound on information leakage from the sender's source can replace a detailed model of the source. The authors show that this bound, quantified by the probability of guessing the input from everything the source emits, suffices to prove security against collective attacks, with no assumptions on the form, dimension, energy or purity of the emitted states. They note that the standard B92 and BB84 protocols cannot certify a key under this assumption, whereas closely related protocols can reach one secret bit per round in the ideal limit. For noisy implementations, key rates are computed with semidefinite programming relaxations, and the best protocols tolerate visibilities down to 0.84, corresponding to an 8% quantum bit error rate, versus the 11% threshold of device-dependent BB84. ★★★★ Notable: Proves security from a single leakage bound without device modeling, reaching near-ideal key rates; validation rests mainly on theory and SDP computations.

entry.title: Experimental evidence that quantum Brownian motion drives electron decoherence in metals
entry.summary: Experimental evidence for quantum Brownian motion in electron-metal decoherence arXiv · Oct 27, 2026 This paper reports experiments showing that quantum Brownian motion plays a key role in the decoherence of electron motion. The authors observe clear signatures of electron-metal decoherence for the first time and show it can be continuously tuned. Agreement between experiment and theory is quantitative, which the authors say paves the way for testing the Caldeira-Leggett dissipation theory with free electrons.

entry.title: Field-deployed entanglement-based BBM92 quantum key distribution using quantum-dot photons converted to telecom wavelengths
entry.summary: Deployed entanglement-based BBM92 quantum key distribution using frequency-converted photons emitted by a quantum dot arXiv · Oct 27, 2026 This paper uses a quantum dot to generate polarization-entangled photon pairs at a 1 GHz excitation rate, then converts them to telecom wavelengths while preserving entanglement. The researchers ran BBM92 quantum key distribution over a 1.59 km field-deployed fibre link at the University of Stuttgart's Vaihingen campus. Over 19 hours of stable operation they achieved a secure key rate of 206 Hz and a total secure key length of 14.2 Mbit, which was used to encrypt and decrypt a colour image.

entry.title: HTM: A Hybrid Model Combining Classical and Quantum Computing
entry.summary: HTM: A Hybrid Classical-Quantum Computation Model arXiv · Oct 27, 2026 This paper addresses the lack of a unified hybrid model for collaborative classical and quantum computation. It proposes HTM, a hybrid classical-quantum computation model built on unified state sets and transition function representations. The model clarifies hybrid control logic, implements a control-sharing mechanism, and introduces a complexity calculation method based on entanglement and superposition to support task partitioning and resource scheduling.

entry.title: Quantum circuits for elastic wave equations using Schrödingerisation
entry.summary: Quantum circuits of elastic wave equations via Schrödingerisation arXiv · Oct 27, 2026 This paper builds explicit quantum circuits for the velocity-stress form of elastic wave equations in homogeneous media, using Schrödingerisation. The equations are rewritten in symmetric matrix form, with Fourier spectral discretization for periodic problems and staggered-grid finite differences for physical boundaries. The authors analyze splitting errors and CNOT-gate counts for higher-order Trotter-Suzuki formulas and compare with classical partitioned splitting, finding a polynomial improvement in spatial-resolution dependence. Noiseless circuit simulations illustrate the constructions and quantify errors against exact and classical reference solutions.

entry.title: QNETSIM: A Simulator for Designing Satellite and Hybrid Quantum Networks with Memory
entry.summary: QNETSIM for memory assisted design of satellite and hybrid quantum networks arXiv · Oct 27, 2026 The paper introduces QNETSIM, a modular discrete-event simulator for designing and evaluating satellite and hybrid space-ground quantum networks. It combines orbital geometry, free-space optical and fiber channels, quantum memories, entanglement generation, and Bell-state measurements in one event-driven framework. The simulator models optical loss, atmospheric turbulence, detector imperfections, finite memory capacity, and storage decoherence. It links these components to entanglement fidelity, throughput, latency, availability, and memory utilization.

entry.title: Threshold conditions for boson and fermion three-body bound states on a square lattice
entry.summary: Threshold Criteria for Bosonic and Fermionic Trimers on a Square Lattice: A Birman--Schwinger Comparison arXiv · Oct 27, 2026 The paper compares two three-particle models on a square lattice at zero total quasimomentum: three identical bosons with attractive contact interactions, and two fermions plus one distinguishable particle with attractive interspecies contact. It uses the Birman–Schwinger principle with symmetry reduction and strong-coupling asymptotics to separate shared methods from model-specific spectral results. For bosons, exactly two bound states lie below threshold at large coupling, the second being a true eigenvalue 0.03542 below threshold. For fermions, the critical mass ratio is π/(π−2), about 2.75194, above which a doubly degenerate level appears at strong coupling.

entry.title: Matrix samplers and quantum-proof extractors: equivalence and near-optimal constructions
entry.summary: Matrix Samplers and Quantum-Proof Extractors: Their Correspondence and Almost-Optimal Constructions arXiv · Oct 27, 2026 The paper establishes an equivalence between matrix samplers and quantum-proof randomness extractors, extending Zuckerman's classical sampler-extractor correspondence. Using this equivalence, the authors construct explicit strong matrix samplers with optimal randomness overhead and near-optimal sample complexity. They also obtain strong quantum-proof extractors with improved seed and output lengths. ★★★★ Notable: Establishes equivalence between matrix samplers and quantum-proof extractors, improving sample complexity and seed length over prior matrix samplers.

entry.title: Quantum generative model that trains only a linear output layer, not the circuit
entry.summary: Generative quantum extreme learning machines arXiv · Oct 27, 2026 The paper proposes a quantum generative method that encodes a random latent vector into a quantum state, applies a fixed unitary and measures, training only a linear output layer so the circuit itself is never trained. Using Pauli propagation, the authors show that Clifford circuits do not create new functions, while Haar-random brickwork circuits have features whose variation with the latent variable decreases with depth. Across one- and two-dimensional distributions, entangling reservoirs do not systematically improve the generator, and a reservoir with no gates performs competitively.

entry.title: Time needed to confirm weak-force entanglement between levitated particles
entry.summary: Certification Time for Weak-Force-Mediated Entanglement between Levitated Particles arXiv · Oct 27, 2026 This paper studies how to certify motional entanglement generated by weak forces between levitated nanoparticles using finite, noisy measurement records. The authors derive a lower bound on the number of measurements needed to certify Gaussian entanglement and translate it into certification time. They compare release-recapture and continuous monitoring protocols, finding that release-recapture enables certification at interaction strengths several orders of magnitude weaker.

entry.title: Quantum Fisher information deficit as a geometric sign of strong-to-weak symmetry breaking
entry.summary: Quantum Fisher Information Deficit as a Geometric Signature of Strong-to-Weak Spontaneous Symmetry Breaking arXiv · Oct 27, 2026 The paper studies strong-to-weak spontaneous symmetry breaking (SW-SSB), a phase of open quantum systems that conventional charged two-point correlators cannot detect. For strongly Z2-symmetric states with local charged involutions, the authors show that SW-SSB appears as a persistent gap between the quantum Fisher information and its maximum under symmetry-neutral pair rotations. This deficit is shown to be equivalent to fidelity and Rényi-1 correlator diagnostics of asymptotic long-range order, and a lower bound is derived for symmetry-projected Gibbs states.

entry.title: Exact decoherence of a detector in bounded vacuum geometries
entry.summary: Exact decoherence dynamics of a detector coupled to vacuum fluctuations in bounded geometries arXiv · Oct 27, 2026 This paper studies how a two-level detector coupled to a vacuum scalar field loses coherence over time in three settings: free space, a single perfectly reflecting boundary, and a cavity between two parallel reflecting boundaries. The authors derive an exact decoherence function for the detector. Coherence decays monotonically in free space, partially persists with one boundary, and oscillates with a larger surviving fraction inside the cavity. The results suggest that boundary conditions can be used to engineer quantum coherence.

entry.title: Using quantum annealing to detect and locate gamma-ray sources in AGILE data
entry.summary: Quantum Annealing for Gamma-ray Source Detection and Localization with AGILE Data arXiv · Oct 27, 2026 This paper reformulates maximum-likelihood gamma-ray source detection and localization as a Quadratic Unconstrained Binary Optimization (QUBO) problem and solves it with simulated quantum annealing. The method is applied to simulated observations from AGILE's Gamma-Ray Imaging Detector in the 30 MeV to 50 GeV band, generated with AGILEpy. The flux and position estimates agree with classical results within statistical uncertainty, and the correct grid node is identified in 97% of the maps.

entry.title: Making the TEMPO network independent of system size
entry.summary: The TEMPO network can be made independent of the system size arXiv · Oct 27, 2026 The TEMPO method simulates non-Markovian open quantum system dynamics by contracting a two-dimensional tensor network. The paper shows that, within the usual second-order time-step error, all internal bond dimensions can be reduced to (2m+1)(m+1), where m is the number of independent coupling channels. This dimension does not depend on the number of distinct eigenvalues of the coupling operators. System size enters only through the final boundary layer, making large systems accessible to TEMPO.

entry.title: Quantum entanglement in momentum space after Kaluza-Klein reduction
entry.summary: Momentum-space entanglement and mutual information in Kaluza-Klein reduction arXiv · Oct 27, 2026 This paper studies how a four-dimensional observer's reduced state, obtained by tracing out massive Kaluza-Klein modes of a five-dimensional scalar with cubic or quartic self-interaction, is entangled in momentum space. At leading order in the coupling, it computes the mutual information between low-energy zero modes and a single Kaluza-Klein level, finding a tail that falls as one over the level mass in the cubic theory. The authors conclude that the local four-dimensional effective theory describes low-energy observables but not the state of the reduced system.

entry.title: Quantum evolution kernel for embedding attributed graphs on neutral-atom computers
entry.summary: Quantum Evolution Kernel for Node-Attributed Graphs arXiv · Oct 27, 2026 This paper proposes a way to embed node-attributed graphs on neutral-atom quantum computers and applies it to digit recognition. It extends PASQAL's quantum evolution kernel with a node-level encoding based on three-level quantum states, and uses the resulting correlation-based information for classification. The quantum process is simulated with the Pulser library, which limits dataset size. On digit recognition, the method using the Wasserstein distance achieves higher mean accuracy than commonly used Jensen-Shannon distance-based methods.

entry.title: Circuit-aware mutation testing for quantum programs: exact visibility and execution planning
entry.summary: Toward Circuit-Aware Mutation Testing for Quantum Programs: Exact Visibility and Execution Planning arXiv · Oct 27, 2026 This paper proposes a circuit-aware framework for mutation testing of quantum programs, distinguishing whether surviving mutants leave behavior unchanged, are hidden by input or measurement choices, or lack sufficient statistical evidence. It targets ideal, noiseless programs with mutations that replace one gate or subcircuit, combining mathematical checks with statistical estimates. For supported cases, it gives conditions under which a test cannot reveal a mutation and exact effect formulas, along with a decision procedure, guarantees, and a small-circuit reference implementation.

entry.title: Quantum and Classical Memory Needed to Store and Retrieve Quantum Measurements
entry.summary: Quantum and Classical Memory for Storage and Retrieval of Quantum Measurements arXiv · Oct 27, 2026 This paper studies how much persistent quantum and classical memory is needed to store and retrieve quantum measurements exactly and with heralding. Assuming only black-box access to the measurement channel, the authors compress a port-based program into an outcome-type record and a quantum register whose total dimension grows polynomially with the number of queries. For n-outcome POVMs on C^d with d ≥ 2, they prove lower bounds Q+C ≥ log₂n and 2Q+C ≥ log₂((n−1)d²+1) on the qubits Q and bits C of any retrieval program.

entry.title: From QCCD trapped-ion hardware to quantum compilers: architectures and compilation methods
entry.summary: From QCCD Trapped-Ion Hardware to Quantum Compilers: Capabilities, Architectures, and Compilation arXiv · Oct 27, 2026 This paper examines shuttling-based trapped-ion quantum computers (QCCD) and their compilers, abstracting QCCD architectures and native operations so that computer scientists can address compilation problems without deep knowledge of the platform's physics. The design space is organized into a few architectural archetypes, and compilation methods are applied to one- and two-dimensional QCCD architectures. Routing overhead is found to scale roughly cubically with qubit number in one dimension and roughly quadratically in two dimensions. The authors also compare physical and logical levels when a quantum error-correction layer is added, and conclude that hardware-software co-design is required.

entry.title: Correlation-sensitive magic-state distillation from spin-squeezed neutral atoms
entry.summary: Correlation-sensitive magic-state distillation from spin-squeezed neutral atoms arXiv · Oct 27, 2026 The paper shows that correlations between blocks can reverse magic-state distillation gain even when each input exceeds the independent-state threshold. Using the five-to-one Bravyi-Kitaev protocol, it expresses the output through measurable target-axis moments and gives a direct sign test for gain. It links this mechanism to neutral-atom resource preparation via finite-range Ising dynamics.

entry.title: Entanglement between a qubit and its environment during pure dephasing when the qubit starts mixed
entry.summary: Qubit-environment entanglement in pure dephasing dynamics for mixed initial states arXiv · Oct 27, 2026 The paper studies entanglement between a qubit and its environment under interactions that cause pure dephasing, allowing the qubit's initial state to be mixed. The authors find that separability criteria valid for pure initial states reduce to entanglement witnesses in this setting. Using a spin qubit coupled to a sparse spin environment as an example, they illustrate the evolution of entanglement and note that witnesses are numerically more practical for large environments.

entry.title: Open effective field theories: a framework for noisy, dissipative environments in gravity and cosmology
entry.summary: The Disordered Universe 2025: Open Effective Field Theories arXiv · Oct 27, 2026 These are lecture notes on Open Effective Field Theories, based on lectures given at the La Ricotta Summer School "The Disordered Universe 2025". The text notes that traditional effective field theories were developed for particle physics with clean, isolated initial states, while realistic environments are often noisy and dissipative. It presents an approach that models the gravitational sector as evolving in the presence of an unobservable medium, and uses the Schwinger-Keldysh formalism to show how unknown environments appear as dissipation and noise in observational probes.

entry.title: A unified six-step protocol for arbitrary Z rotations on a class of bosonic cQED qubits
entry.summary: A Unified Protocol for Arbitrary Z Rotations of a Class of Bosonic cQED Qubits arXiv · Oct 27, 2026 This paper examines a class of bosonic Fock-based qubits in circuit QED and shows that different ways of implementing arbitrary Z rotations on them share a common structure. The authors formulate this structure as a six-step protocol that gives a unified procedure for arbitrary Z rotations across this qubit class. Whether the protocol applies depends on a specific condition on the encoding, which serves as a criterion for identifying which bosonic Fock-based cQED qubits admit this common implementation.

entry.title: Storing and extracting energy in V-type quantum batteries via dark states
entry.summary: Controlled Dark-State Energy Storage and Work Extraction in V-Type Quantum Batteries arXiv · Oct 27, 2026 This paper studies a quantum battery made of V-type qutrits coupled to a lossy cavity. A finite splitting pulse converts cavity-bright excitations into atomic dark states, which keep their stored energy even after degeneracy is restored. The authors also bound the passive energy in the symmetric atomic subspace and compare coherent and Fock initial states for finite-time ergotropy and extractable work.

entry.title: Lifting Quasi-Cyclic Additive Codes to Certified Quantum Codes
entry.summary: Ancestor Lifting of Quasi-Cyclic Additive Codes and Certified Quantum Codes arXiv · Oct 27, 2026 This paper studies additive codes over F4 that correspond to binary quantum stabilizer codes, focusing on 1-generator (1,2)-quasi-cyclic additive codes. It gives an ancestor-lifting theorem for composite lengths, dimension laws, and a palindromic criterion for symplectic self-orthogonality. Exact quantum distances are determined through information-set decoding screening, Brouwer–Zimmermann computation, and independent witness verification. The authors certify a set of record-breaking binary quantum codes and report further propagated entries and upper bounds.

entry.title: Quantum state preparation for complex amplitudes
entry.summary: Quantum State Preparation for Complex-Valued Amplitudes arXiv · Oct 27, 2026 This paper presents a procedure that prepares a quantum amplitude approximating z/α for a complex number z=x+iy, starting from registers holding its real and imaginary parts, with α a normalization constant. It computes the magnitude and argument with the CORDIC algorithm, encodes the magnitude into an amplitude, and applies phase gates for the argument. The method uses O(n²) T gates and O(n) extra qubits. Compared with encoding real and imaginary parts separately and combining them via LCU, it can allow a smaller normalization and reduce amplitude-amplification costs.

entry.title: Diagnostic-dependent lasting Mpemba effect in a parametrically driven oscillator
entry.summary: Diagnostic-dependent lasting Mpemba effect in a parametrically driven oscillator arXiv · Oct 27, 2026 This paper studies relaxation of two Gaussian states in a detuned degenerate parametric amplifier below threshold. The trace distance shows a lasting Mpemba reversal, while relative entropy eventually restores the initial order and Hilbert-Schmidt distance alternates indefinitely. The three diagnostics agree on the initial order but can disagree because a real mode and a complex pair share the leading decay rate.

entry.title: Kinetic Slush in Dissipative Rydberg Arrays: a nonequilibrium soft-matter state in driven atom arrays
entry.summary: Kinetic Slush in Dissipative Rydberg Arrays arXiv · Oct 27, 2026 The paper studies a kinetic slush state in a two-dimensional dissipative Rydberg atom array, where excitations are facilitated by neighboring atoms. Using kinetic Monte Carlo simulations in the strong dephasing regime, the authors show that detuning compensates nearest-neighbor interactions, while residual next-nearest-neighbor interactions create kinetic frustration. The competition yields a slush phase with liquid- and solid-like configurations and strong dynamical heterogeneity.

entry.title: Noise thresholds for reliable quantum approximate optimisation under noise
entry.summary: Effective Noise Thresholds for Reliable Quantum Approximation Optimisation Algorithm under Noisy Environment arXiv · Oct 27, 2026 This paper studies how much noise the quantum approximate optimisation algorithm (QAOA) can tolerate at each circuit depth. The authors run GPU-accelerated noisy simulations on MaxCut for three graph families and fit approximation ratios with a generalised logistic surface. They define an effective noise threshold, which generally decreases as depth increases, and use it to separate reliable from unreliable noise regimes.

entry.title: Measurement-induced entanglement phases in hyperbolic gauge-Higgs models
entry.summary: Measurement-induced entanglement phases in hyperbolic gauge-Higgs models arXiv · Oct 27, 2026 This paper studies entanglement phases of gauge-Higgs models on hyperbolic lattices, described by measurement-only dynamics. The authors map two-dimensional phase diagrams using topological entanglement entropy and a generalized measurement-induced entanglement suited to hyperbolic Higgs phases. They identify an "archipelago" phase absent in Euclidean space, where separated clusters of symmetry-protected topological order exist, and its transitions have mean-field critical exponents.

entry.title: Fewest Measurement Settings for Estimating Several Quantum Observables
entry.summary: Minimal Projective Measurement Settings for Estimating Multiple Observables arXiv · Oct 27, 2026 This paper studies the minimum number of orthogonal projective measurement settings needed to estimate several observables without bias for any input state. The authors derive structural lower bounds beyond dimension counting and give explicit constructions that certify minimum setting counts for chosen target spaces. A classical variational algorithm searches for shared measurement bases and optimizes readout coefficients and sample allocation. For the collective first and second moments of two qubits, four projective settings are shown to be both necessary and sufficient.

entry.title: Unusual shapes of Fisher zero lines in biorthogonal dynamical quantum phase transitions
entry.summary: Anomalous Structures of Fisher Zero Lines in Biorthogonal Dynamical Quantum Phase Transitions arXiv · Oct 27, 2026 This paper studies how Fisher zero lines of the Loschmidt amplitude in non-Hermitian quenches can form unusual patterns in the complex time plane, such as divergence, separation, or branches lying on the real or imaginary axis. It uses a biorthogonal framework to explain these patterns and sets critical momentum conditions based on the dot product of normalized prequench and postquench complex Bloch vectors. The results are verified in a generalized non-Hermitian SSH model, and Jordan form is used to analyze dynamics at postquench exceptional points.

entry.title: Dynamical behaviour of the mass tensor in the lattice
entry.summary: Dynamical behaviour of the mass tensor in the lattice arXiv · Oct 27, 2026 This paper studies, with a semiclassical model, how a particle hopping through an orthorhombic lattice moves under a static Coulomb field and a rapidly oscillating homogeneous field. Applying the oscillating field reparameterizes the effective masses so they become equal in both directions, turning a chaotic trajectory into an elliptic one in the continuum limit, as confirmed by Lyapunov exponents. The authors also show that an external magnetic field along the Z direction can control chaos, and extend the scheme to three-dimensional trajectories.

entry.title: Coherent optical control of a single donor electron spin
entry.summary: Coherent Optical Control of a Single Donor Electron Spin arXiv · Oct 27, 2026 This paper demonstrates optical initialization, coherent control, and readout of a single donor-bound electron spin in ZnSe. Using spin-selective donor-bound exciton transitions and off-resonant picosecond pulses, the authors observe spin Rabi oscillations, Ramsey interference, and high-contrast coherent population trapping. At higher driving strengths, multiple dark resonances reveal the hyperfine interaction with the I = 3/2 Cl nucleus, and the authors identify isolated optical donors as a promising platform for solid-state optically active qubits. ★★★★ Notable: First coherent optical control of a single donor electron spin in a II-VI semiconductor, with coherent population trapping and hyperfine resolution.

entry.title: Analytic energy formulas for radial power-like potentials via new Bohr-Sommerfeld quantization conditions
entry.summary: Radial power-like potentials: from the Bohr-Sommerfeld ℓ ≠ 0 state energies to the exact ones arXiv · Oct 27, 2026 The paper proposes two new Bohr-Sommerfeld type quantization conditions for d-dimensional radial singular and non-singular potentials. It studies power-like potentials and the logarithmic potential across many radial quantum numbers and angular momenta in dimensions two and three. For large radial quantum numbers the approximate energies approach the exact ones, and a dimensionless WKB correction reproduces exact energies within the cases examined.

entry.title: Sideways position shift of a spinning particle's wave packet under Lorentz boosts
entry.summary: Side jump and anomalous Lorentz transformation of a coherent Dirac wave packet arXiv · Oct 27, 2026 This paper studies how spin-orbit coupling makes the average position of a spinning particle shift unusually under a Lorentz boost, an effect called a side jump. The authors develop a trace method that yields an exact, compact transformation kernel for the probability center of a general three-dimensional Dirac wave packet under any finite boost, without a semiclassical expansion. They find that side jumps depend on the wave packet's internal structure and that, for Gaussian packets, they show a non-monotonic dependence on mass.

entry.title: Consensus and information spreading in quantum networks: how nodes learn global quantum information from local measurements
entry.summary: Consensus And Information Redistribution In Quantum Networks arXiv · Oct 27, 2026 This paper studies decentralized quantum consensus in qudit networks evolving under discrete random unitary dynamics. The authors analyze asymptotic behavior, identify global information preserved by the evolution, and give conditions under which different forms of quantum consensus arise. They present a general theorem for extracting globally encoded information from local measurements, examine CNOT networks, and identify two-qubit interactions that asymptotically reach consensus on average excitation number.

entry.title: Finite-temperature quantum theory of lossy magnon-cavity resonators
entry.summary: Finite-temperature Quantum Quasinormal Mode Theory for Spatiotemporally-resolved Dissipative Cavity Quantum Magnonics arXiv · Oct 27, 2026 This paper develops a finite-temperature quantum quasinormal mode (QNM) theory for cavity magnonic systems containing non-reciprocal magnetic media, material dissipation, open-cavity radiation losses and thermal fluctuations. It uses macroscopic quantum electrodynamics and complex coordinate transformations to quantize the QNMs. The authors apply the theory to hybrid dielectric-magnonic resonators coupled to spin and superconducting qubits, showing modal interference, a transition from coherent to dissipative coupling, and magnon-mediated qubit synchronization.

entry.title: Suppressing microwave crosstalk in superconducting quantum processors by designing parasitic capacitances
entry.summary: Suppressing microwave crosstalk in superconducting quantum processors by designing parasitic drive capacitances arXiv · Oct 27, 2026 This paper studies how unwanted microwave drive crosstalk between qubits in a superconducting quantum processor can be reduced. The authors build a detailed circuit model of a processor with two fixed-frequency transmon qubits and a tunable coupler, and experimentally show that crosstalk can be suppressed. They find the suppression comes not only from cancelling the effective qubit-qubit coupling but also from interference among other coupling paths. The authors conclude that choosing suitable parasitic capacitances can suppress crosstalk, suggesting that parasitic coupling paths should be engineered rather than simply minimized.

entry.title: Multi-day magnetic imaging of single living cancer cells using a quantum sensor
entry.summary: Multi-day single-cell magnetic imaging of living cancer cells using Quantum Cell Monitoring arXiv · Oct 27, 2026 This paper presents Quantum Cell Monitoring (QCM), a widefield nitrogen-vacancy magnetometry platform that records single-cell information from stray magnetic fields instead of emitted photons, at subcellular resolution. Combined with a live-cell incubator, it tracks magnetically labeled living cancer cells for up to 72 hours. The authors report observing mitosis, morphological changes, and cluster formation, splitting, and migration.
